generated_by: MES-68 (A3) — hand-run extraction, procedure below. NOT a mix task: the input is a /tmp harness build, so a task would be unrunnable on any tree where that build is absent.
polarity_rule: Every axis carries `polarity` — `pass_when_true` (the expr being TRUE means the requirement is MET) or `fail_when_true` (TRUE means it is VIOLATED) — and a `polarity_reading` naming the branch of the row's OWN `evaluator_excerpt` that decides it. IT IS AUTHORED, NOT DERIVED, and that is a measured decision rather than a stylistic one: a classifier keying on `===` versus `!==` returns 5 / 14 / 1-undecidable over these 20 axes, because `sep-2106-no-network-ref-deref` axis `canary_not_fetched` has expr `this.canaryRequests.length>0` and contains NEITHER operator. A derived polarity would therefore be absent on exactly the row nobody would think to check. `requires` carries the human reading and always did; `polarity` is what a consumer computing a verdict FROM `expr` needs.

polarity_totals.checked_by: test/conformance/match_key_test.exs — totals recomputed from the per-axis values and compared as a SET against the 20, so a total that drifts from the rows cannot pass
polarity_totals.why_the_split_is_not_random: The split falls along the 7/5 call-site line: the `===` idiom writes the PASS condition, the `!==`/`||` idiom writes the FAIL condition. Two harness authoring styles, not randomness.

preconditions_rule: Every check carries `preconditions` as a LIST OF OBJECTS `{guard, on_failure, reads, kind}`. `guard` and `on_failure` are VERBATIM SUBSTRINGS of that row's own `evaluator_excerpt` — the same discipline `expr` already keeps — so the field can be checked rather than believed. `kind` is `network` (the probe did not complete) or `semantic` (the probe completed but the requirement is not evaluable). `[]` IS NOT A LEGAL VALUE, and a test enforces it. Before MES-76, 5 of the 13 rows recorded `[]` while having guards of exactly the shape the other 8 did record, so `[]` read as "checked, and none" when it meant "not recorded". A row that genuinely has no guard must say so with an explicit sentinel entry (`kind: "none"`, sole entry in its row) — so that silence cannot encode the answer. No row in this artefact currently needs the sentinel: all 13 have at least one guard.

authoring_procedure: DIRECTION: axis -> site. This is how the 13 rows below were actually CUT, and it is kept for that reason. It is NOT the path a consumer travels: its step 1 presupposes you already know the axis expression, which is the thing a consumer is trying to find. A3 could write it this way because A3 already had the answers. For the consumer's direction see `reverse_lookup_procedure`.
1. Locate the axis expression verbatim in the dist. Each of the seven used here occurs EXACTLY ONCE in the file, so the location is unambiguous.
2. Walk back to the nearest enclosing `a(` check-emitting call (or, for the client-leg class-based scenario, the enclosing `getChecks(){`).
3. Balanced-scan forward to the matching close, honouring ' " ` string contexts and ${} template nesting, and record the span.
4. `evaluator_excerpt` is that span verbatim; `dist_byte_span` addresses it in the file named by `harness_dist_sha256`, so any reader with that build can re-cut it.
provenance.equals_manifest_harness_dist_sha256: both legs — docs/conformance/in-scope-2026-07-28.json provenance.server and provenance.client carry this same sha, so these axes are read from the exact build behind the accepted runs, not a lookalike
provenance.residual: Committed axes are a READING OF A PREDICATE AT ONE BUILD. A harness bump invalidates them exactly as A1's residual R3 says it invalidates keys. The sha is recorded so a reader can tell whether it has been invalidated; nothing here detects it automatically.

cases.0_occurrences_TEMPLATE: THE GREP RETURNED NOTHING. You are in the template case — you are NOT looking at a missing check, and you must NOT fall back to reading the check's `description`. The id is BUILT at runtime, e.g. ``a(`sep-2575-http-server-method-not-found-404-${t}`,...)``. Grep instead for the LONGEST LITERAL PREFIX of the id (drop trailing segments until the grep hits): for the five 404 rows that prefix is `sep-2575-http-server-method-not-found-404-`, which occurs EXACTLY ONCE and lands directly on the loop's emitting call. Then read the loop's iteration values to recover which concrete ids it produces.
cases.1_occurrence_LITERAL_or_CONSTANT: One hit. If it sits in the FIRST argument position of an `a(` call, that IS the emitting site (form `literal`). If instead it sits on the right of an assignment to a minified name — e.g. ``Za=`sep-2106-no-network-ref-deref` `` — you are in the CONSTANT case and the hit is the BINDING, not the site: take the bound name and grep THAT (`id:Za`) to reach the emitting site. One hit does not by itself mean you have found the site.
cases.2_occurrences_LITERAL_PLUS_PREFIX: Two hits, and they are not duplicates. This happens when one check's id is a PREFIX of another's template: `sep-2575-http-server-method-not-found-404` occurs both as its own literal id and as the prefix inside ``sep-2575-http-server-method-not-found-404-${t}``. Disambiguate by what follows the id: a closing backtick means this check's own site; a `-${` means you have landed on the template loop belonging to a DIFFERENT check.

reverse_lookup_procedure.direction: check_id -> emitting site -> predicate -> axes. This is the direction a consumer travels, and the FIRST hop is the hard one: a grep on the check_id reaches the emitting site for only 7 of the 13 rows.
reverse_lookup_procedure.measured_at: 18df3a6, against harness_dist_sha256 — the occurrence counts in each row's `emitting_site.locator` were re-measured there, not copied forward.
reverse_lookup_procedure.step_0_if_the_row_is_already_here: If the check_id is one of the 13 below, SKIP THE TRAVERSAL ENTIRELY. Read `emitting_site.dist_byte_span` (or `dist_char_span`) and cut that range out of the file named by `harness_dist_sha256`. Measured at 18df3a6 against that build: all 13 rows re-cut BYTE-IDENTICAL to their committed `evaluator_excerpt` on BOTH span kinds, 26 of 26 comparisons. The reverse lookup for a known row is therefore a constant-time cut, not a search.
reverse_lookup_procedure.step_1_branch_on_form: For a check_id NOT below, grep the dist for it and branch on the occurrence count. `emitting_site.form` tells you which of the three cases a KNOWN row is in; for an unknown one the occurrence count tells you, by the rules in `cases`.
reverse_lookup_procedure.step_2_site_to_axes: From the emitting site, the predicate is the arrow function passed as the `a(` call's fourth argument (or, on the client leg's class-based scenario, the object literal returned by `getChecks(){`). Decompose it per `axis_source_rule`: axes come from the PREDICATE, never from the description. Each axis's `expr` is a verbatim substring of the excerpt, and its `polarity` says which way the expression reads.
reverse_lookup_procedure.why_this_is_not_a_mix_task: The input is a /tmp harness build, so a task would be unrunnable on any tree where that build is absent — the same reasoning `generated_by` already gives, unchanged. A written procedure plus the recorded spans is the deliverable.

scope.rule: The checks A3's ruling is computed from: the 12 `server-stateless` FAILURE checks whose own errorMessage carries an HTTP status (the R2 class the epic sized at 12), plus the client-leg CG4 counterpart used as AC3's worked example.
scope.why_not_all_175: An axis decomposition is only consumed where an edge exists, and the edge set is C1's (PM amendment 2). Decomposing all 175 here would be A3 building C1's artefact — the MES-24 two-owners defect — and 162 of them would be built before anyone knows which have an ET counterpart at all.

the_7_5_split.claim: A3's partial-axis ruling moves at most 7 of the 12, not 12. The other 5 move the OTHER way — into bucket 2, 'write the test', not 'extend the assertion'.
the_7_5_split.reasoning: For a SINGLE-axis check, 'we assert the code but not the status' is NO match, not a partial one: covering zero of one axis has nothing partial about it, and the code assertion is evidence about a DIFFERENT check (`RequestMetaInvalid`, `ServerUnsupportedVersionError`, `ServerRejectsUndeclaredCapability`), which is why those three also appear among server-stateless's 17 failures. Recording it as partial would credit us with coverage filed elsewhere.
the_7_5_split.status: PROVISIONAL. The OC side is measured here; the ET side is not swept until B2a. MES-65's 'A3's partial-axis ruling alone moves 12 checks between buckets' is superseded by this and the PM will correct the epic body once B2a confirms.

what_this_is: The per-check AXIS DECOMPOSITION the match relation's `partial` ruling is computed from. An OC check's predicate is a conjunction of axes; against each axis an ET claim is exactly one of agrees/contradicts/silent. This file records the axes, each as a verbatim substring of the evaluator it was read from.
